name: Wistia
summary: Video hosting built for marketing — player customisation, viewer analytics and lead capture.
best_for: marketing teams who want video on their own site with real analytics and lead capture, and who care that the player does not recommend a competitor's video afterwards
skip_if: you just need somewhere to put videos — an unlisted upload to a free platform does that, and the reason to pay here is the analytics and the branding control, not the hosting
honest_knock: Bandwidth is the meter that decides your bill, and it is the one number you cannot predict before you publish. A single video that does well can move you from Free to Business in a month, which is arguably the product working — but budget for it rather than being surprised. Their FAQ is precise about which way it cuts: free accounts cannot exceed their bandwidth limit, while paid plans are billed for usage beyond what is included or prepaid. The free tier carries Wistia branding on the player, so it is a trial with no time limit rather than a plan you can ship a brand on. The published prices are the annual ones; the page's toggle sits on Annual with a 20% saving and the month-to-month figures are not in its source, so a monthly subscriber cannot price the plan from the pricing page. The webinar overages are the sharpest edge: $2.00 per extra minute means a session that runs long costs real money, the allowance is per event rather than cumulative, and both facts are in the FAQ rather than on the pricing card.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-19 on wistia.com/pricing, Video Platform tab; the monthly rates below were read with the page's billing toggle set to Monthly) Four tiers, and the headline numbers are the ANNUAL rates: the billing toggle on the page is set to Annual with a “Save 20%” chip, so Business at $79 a month and Business + Lead gen at $329 a month are what you pay when you commit for a year. Switch that toggle to Monthly and the same three cards read $0, $99 and $412 a month, with the per-extra-user rate moving from $25 to $31 — so the 20% the chip promises is real, and paying month to month costs about a fifth more. Those monthly figures are rendered by the page rather than written in its source, which is why they can only be read with a browser. Free $0: 25 GB storage, 1 user, 200 GB bandwidth, basic analytics, Wistia branding on the player. Business $79: 250 GB+ storage, 3 users, 1 TB bandwidth, branding removed, collections and playlists, in-video CTAs and forms, advanced analytics. Business + Lead gen $329 is Business plus the Automation Suite — marketing-platform connection (HubSpot, Adobe Marketo Engage, Pardot), lead capture and scoring, pipeline measurement — and the FAQ describes that suite as something you add to a Business plan rather than a separate product. Enterprise is quote-only: from 1 TB storage, 2 TB bandwidth, custom users, unlimited view-only access, team accounts, SSO, video playback protection, a dedicated customer success manager. Price per additional user $25. Three rows in the feature table carry a “$” instead of a tick in every column, Enterprise included: Webinars, AI audio descriptions, and video dubbing with lip syncing. The overage rules sit in the FAQ rather than on the cards. Bandwidth is included with every plan and resets every month; free accounts cannot exceed their limit, while paid plans are billed for usage beyond what is included or prepaid. Storage works the same way and can be bought upfront to avoid usage charges. Users are billed for usage beyond the seats the plan includes, as you add and remove them. Webinar and live-event allowances are per event and not cumulative across events; additional attendees are charged at $0.20 each and additional duration minutes at $2.00 each, billed on the next monthly billing date. You can cancel at any time unless you are on Enterprise or a signed order form, either at the end of the billing cycle or immediately, and no refund is issued either way. Webinar plans have their own tab on the same page and carry no price in the source.

vendor_mcp.what: Server for uploading video, making bulk updates, managing access and reading performance data from your agent. Every action asks for approval by default; you can set a tool to always-approve or block it.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their FAQ: "All Wistia accounts have access to Wistia's MCP server... no upgrade needed." Anything you can do in the app you can do through the server; you only upgrade for more product features. Restricted by role rather than plan — owners and managers only.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
